talks.title: Introduction by Iowa Lt Governor Chris Cournoyer
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Introduction by Iowa Lt Governor Chris Cournoyer.
talks.summary:
Overview:
Iowa Lieutenant Governor Chris Cournoyer delivers the opening keynote address at CornCon 2025 in Davenport, Iowa. Cournoyer frames the conference as a vital catalyst for regional cyber resilience, celebrating the Midwest's growing technology innovation ecosystem known as the "Silicon Prairie." She details coordinated state-level cybersecurity initiatives, critical infrastructure defense programs, and multidisciplinary educational pipelines designed to develop the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.

Key Topics:
- Midwestern technology innovation and the "Silicon Prairie" ecosystem
- Iowa Cybersecurity Resilience Initiative and public sector defense
- NIST Cybersecurity Framework integration and incident management tabletop exercises
- K-12 STEM outreach, Children of the CornCon, and workforce development

Technical Details:
Lieutenant Governor Cournoyer highlights the collaborative role of CornCon in uniting enterprise security leaders, CISOs, subject matter experts, and public sector defenders across the Quad Cities and the greater Midwest. She emphasizes that regional cybersecurity readiness requires structured coordination across municipal, county, and state entities. To operationalize this, the state launched the Iowa Cybersecurity Resilience Initiative, administered through Iowa State University’s Center for Cybersecurity Innovation and Outreach (CIO) and funded by the federal State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program.

The initiative delivers foundational defensive capabilities to vulnerable public sector targets, including cities, counties, and school districts facing persistent threats from ransomware and data breaches. Participating entities receive standardized IT asset inventories to map attack surfaces, risk assessments aligned with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework, and Cybersecurity Incident Management (SCIM) tabletop exercises that simulate crisis decision-making under operational pressure. Cournoyer also announces the state’s inaugural cybersecurity conference scheduled for October 16th to sustain statewide defense momentum.

Addressing the technical workforce shortage, Cournoyer outlines Iowa’s integrated education pipeline spanning K-12 to post-graduate studies. In higher education, Iowa State University serves as a designated National Center of Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity (CAE), offering multidisciplinary programs alongside institutions such as Upper Iowa University, the University of Dubuque, and regional community colleges supported by the Future Ready Iowa Last-Dollar Scholarship. For early engagement, the Governor’s STEM Council drives the STEM BEST program and Project Lead The Way high school cybersecurity curricula. Additionally, youth-focused community initiatives like "Children of the CornCon" provide K-12 students with hands-on technical training in lockpicking, soldering, coding, Google dorking, and capture-the-flag competitions, while practical defenses like YubiKey deployments provide hardware-based multi-factor authentication (MFA) to public school IT staff.

Key Takeaways:
State and local governments must leverage structured frameworks like the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and periodic tabletop exercises to harden municipal infrastructure against ransomware. Establishing robust public-private partnerships and utilizing federal cybersecurity grants enhances defensive capabilities for resource-constrained public sector organizations. Long-term regional resilience requires proactive talent development through early STEM engagement, hands-on security education, and hardware-backed identity protections.

talks.title: CornCon_11 FRI-T1-9:00 - Lyle Kelly - The Current Threat Landscape Requires a Unique Approach
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for CornCon_11 FRI-T1-9:00 - Lyle Kelly - The Current Threat Landscape Requires a Unique Approach.
talks.summary:
Vidair Labs Overview

Lyle Kelly presents threat landscape research from Vidair Labs, a nearly decade-old Idaho research wing. The lab has found nearly 200 original vulnerabilities—59% without CVEs—and runs about 2,000 curated sandbox detonations monthly, publishing free public dashboards.

Research Methodology

Capabilities include malware sandboxes, dark web monitoring via Tor, and adversary lab environments mimicking OT, medical, IoT, and enterprise IT deployments. Honeypots invite attackers so researchers can observe exfiltration and lateral movement behaviors.

Scale of Data Exposure

Kelly cites 1.3 billion individual records leaked to date and a 2.7 billion-record host-data breach from a compromised research firm later dumped free on the dark web after failed sale attempts.

Geographic Threat Trends

Contrary to assumptions, current data shows significant exfiltration originating from U.S. infrastructure, with Russia recently leading in some metrics. Attackers abuse global hosting to launch campaigns from unexpected locations.

talks.title: CornCon_11 FRI-T2-9:00 David Garlak & Jon Schnell Chasing SSRF in Downstream Asynchronous Workflows
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning CornCon_11 FRI-T2-9:00 David Garlak & Jon Schnell Chasing SSRF in Downstream Asynchronous Workflows.
talks.summary:
SSRF Basics

David Garlak and Jon Schnell of Rapid7 define server-side request forgery as an injection point where the server fetches attacker-chosen URLs—acting as a proxy to internal or external resources. Variants include open redirects, file/SMB schemes, weak credentials, and cloud metadata misconfigurations.

Transparency Levels

They categorize transparent SSRF (attacker sees full response), semi-blind (DNS or partial hits only), and blind SSRF (no outbound visibility, requiring side channels). These labels frame later discussion of asynchronous workflows.

Defense Layers

Mitigations start with strict URL allowlisting—not denylisting—and careful URI parsing quirks. Response validation matters: teams often validate inbound input but trust fetched content. Network isolation and tight egress filtering reduce semi-blind callbacks.

Async Workflow Angle

The core topic is SSRF in downstream asynchronous jobs—webhooks, profile image fetchers, and background tasks where the request and response are decoupled. Attackers abuse delayed or blind fetches where traditional synchronous SSRF testing fails, demanding correlation across job queues and egress logs.

talks.title: CornCon_11 FRI-T3-9:45 Barry Suskind
talks.teaser: Successfully Building examines CornCon_11 FRI-T3-9:45 Barry Suskind.
talks.summary:
Purpose of tabletops

Barry Suskind at CornCon, drawing on three decades in security and SANS/Golden Institute work, frames tabletop exercises as dry-run disaster recovery for cyber incidents. They reveal gaps, stress-test teams, and teach containment of information flow so breaches are not discussed over open email or ticketing systems that could tip attackers or leak to the public.

Exercise types

Technical tabletops gather CISOs, engineers, and adjacent staff to walk through realistic scenarios inspired by current news such as ransomware. Business tabletops assume breach declaration and train executives on messaging, regulatory reporting, and crisis decisions. Combined end-to-end runs expose both sides but are hard to schedule because executives rarely sit for multi-hour sessions.

Planning essentials

Suskind recommends two- to four-hour formats, current incident response plans with accurate tooling and contact lists, clear incident command (CISO as liaison, not sole commander), separate defensive and investigative leads, and advance scheduling. He contrasts poor CrowdStrike CTO communications with stronger CEO messaging after the July outage as a lesson in public response.

talks.title: CornCon_11 FRI-T1-9:45 CISO Panel: Kevin Novak, Bruce Phillips, Paul Rice
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for CornCon_11 FRI-T1-9:45 CISO Panel: Kevin Novak, Bruce Phillips, Paul Rice.
talks.summary:
## Overview
CornCon's self-moderated CISO "ask me anything" panel (one speaker absent) shares candid views from practitioners in banking, legal, and enterprise security.

## Daily Challenges
Incident prioritization and triage dominate when every alert isn't equal. No two days match a Franklin Planner—fires constantly displace planned work. One CISO notes aerospace discipline doesn't survive modern security operations.

## Business Integration
Effective CISOs spend more time communicating up and across the business than with technology teams. A long-tenured panelist began by asking the founder "what can I do to help you?" rather than prescribing a security roadmap.

## Takeaways
Leadership, stakeholder trust, and triage judgment matter as much as tooling—invest in relationships before the next incident.
